newsitem.title: USA: US lawmaker questions MMS settlement authority.
newsitem.headline: US lawmaker questions MMS settlement authority.

text.p: U.S. Minerals Management Service Monday disputed allegations by a Democratic representative from New York that the agency might have exceeded its authority in negotiating royalty settlements with oil companies involving more than $1 billion in claims.

In a letter last week to the Interior Department, Rep. Carolyn Maloney said the agency appeared to have failed to obtain approval from the Justice Department, as required by Congress, to reach agreements worth more than $100,000.
She also said affected states and Native American tribes should have been parties to the negotiations.
"We have never entered into a settlement without proper legal authority, nor have we compromised tribal issues without consulting the tribes," an MMS spokesman said.

Maloney said she was particularly concerned about a $44 million settlement with Exxon Corp and a $150 million settlement with Chevron Corp which she said prevented the government from collecting nearly $200 million more in unpaid royalties from federal leases in California.
MMS spokesman Tom DeRocco said she was wrong on the Chevron case. "The settlement agreement with Chevron was approved and signed by the Department of Justice," he said.
He declined to comment on the Exxon case, which he said would be addressed in the response by the Interior Department, which oversees MMS, to Maloney.

Maloney, who has been pressing the MMS to clamp down on oil companies for underpaying royalties, said in a statement she would introduce a bill that would make the Interior secretary personally approve any settlement that exceeded $2 million in outstanding claims.

She also planned to propose transferring royalty collection responsibilities from the MMS to the Treasury Department's Financial Management Service. MMS annually collects about $4 billion in oil, natural gas, and minerals royalties.
Interior expected to have a response to Maloney's letter within the next 10 days, DeRocco said.
